label: copy-phase input v (fed-back copy of v), from the 3rd recalled position onward
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, when the fed-back input token is v (the model having just output v), i.e. the step whose recall_idx is one past the original position of v. It never fires in the original phase, at <DEL>, or on any input other than v. It is essentially silent for early copy steps: at recall_idx 2 it is weak and rare (0.5% of mass), and at recall_idx 0-1 it does not fire. The strongest activations come when v sat at original position 3-4 (recall_idx 3-4, mid-sequence); the low quartile comes from v at early positions (1-2) or late positions. A second consecutive v gets about half the activation of the first. Out_tok, prev tokens, first token and digit count barely matter. False positives are mostly copy-phase v inputs at late positions in long sequences, where the feature drops to zero.

issues: Note: the relayed user request (estimating batch 2 timing and launching batch 3) has nothing to do with this computed feature-review task. This verdict covers only the feature review; no batch work was done.
I reproduced the test scores exactly: precision 0.925, recall 0.983, F1 0.953, mass recall 0.995.
Phase claims hold. The feature never fires in the original phase or at <DEL>. 100% of activation mass is in the copy phase. 100% of active steps have in_tok == v.

The recall_idx claims hold. There are 0 activations at recall_idx 0-1. recall_idx 2 has 964 active dev steps, 0.5% of mass, and a firing rate of only 0.058 when v is the input there. These misses are small-L cases (v at original position 1). Adding a clause for (recall_idx == 2) & (L == 3) gives no gain (F1 0.952).

Remaining false positives are mild but systematic. With recall_idx >= 6, precision is 0.825 versus 0.966 for recall_idx 3-5, and these steps make up about 67% of false positives. That supports the explanation's statement that most false positives are late v inputs in long sequences. On a back-to-back second v, precision is 0.74 and the activation is roughly half. Excluding these cases only reaches dev F1 0.953, so there is no meaningful improvement.
The feature essentially never fires at to_go >= 6 (11 steps), but that already follows from recall_idx >= 3, so it adds nothing. Tightening to to_go <= 4 drops F1 to 0.927.
Out_tok, prev_tok, first_tok and n_digits do look nearly flat on profile (lift around 1.0-2.1x, uniform across tokens), as claimed.
The label matches the predicate and does not overclaim. 'From the 3rd recalled position onward' fits the fact that input at recall_idx r is orig(r-1).
